titulo: PepsiCo: $8.9 billion to shareholders, about 1,000 jobs being cut. The math.
descripcion:
PepsiCo, Nov 9, 2026 (Memo, as quoted by Bloomberg): "too much of how we work today remains complex and fragmented"
Bloomberg News reports PepsiCo is eliminating about 1,000 roles in North America. Its North America CEO wrote this in a memo to workers on Nov. 9. The job count comes from Bloomberg's report.

Same year: $8.9 billion to shareholders, 2026 plan, company-wide. $7.9 billion in dividends and $1.0 billion in share repurchases: PepsiCo's full-year 2026 guidance, company-wide.
The math: $8.9 billion planned (2026) ÷ about 1,000 job cuts (Bloomberg) = about $8.9 million planned per job cut. The jobs count is approximate, per Bloomberg.
This is a ratio, not a payment and not a cause: the total returned to shareholders divided by the job count. The $8.9 billion is PepsiCo's own full-year 2026 guidance for cash returns to shareholders, a plan and not money already paid. PepsiCo has not linked the payout to the job cuts, and neither do we. The job count is about 1,000 roles in North America, per Bloomberg.

Complex. Fragmented. Here is the shareholder column. (Our take.)

Sources:
- Bloomberg via Transport Topics, Nov 9, 2026: «Ram Krishnan, the company’s North America CEO, sent a Nov. 9 memo to workers saying that “too much of how we work today remains complex and fragmented.”» and «PepsiCo Inc. is eliminating about 1,000 roles in North America» https://www.ttnews.com/articles/pepsi-cuts-1000-north-america
- PepsiCo Q3 release (SEC), Oct 8, 2026: «Cash Returns to Shareholders (d) $8.9 billion $8.9 billion» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77476/000007747626000050/q320268-kxexhibit991.htm
